paragraphs: Children in care on the Isle of Wight are looked after by the Isle of Wight Council's own fostering service, shown above with the independent agencies that cover the island.

The council recruits through Local Authority Fostering South East, a regional hub it runs with 19 other councils. First enquiries go to the hub, which shares training and support across the region and says its network includes more than 2,800 fostering families in the South East. Once you apply, assessment and ongoing support come from the Isle of Wight's own fostering team.

During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026 the council said it is always looking for new carers for emergency, short-term and longer-term fostering. It stressed that you do not need to own your home or be married: the essentials are a spare room and the ability to give a child a loving, stable home. Its carers receive training, professional support and financial allowances.

The island is in the South East band of the national minimum allowance, which every fostering service in England must pay at least. For 2026-27 that is £195 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £203 for ages 3 to 4, £223 for ages 5 to 10, £255 for ages 11 to 15 and £298 for ages 16 to 17. Many services pay more, often with a fee for the carer on top, so ask each one what it pays and what it expects.

Speak to two or three of the services above, including the council, about the children who most need homes on the island, the training on offer and how support and training work for carers living on the island.
